proposals.title: BC-07's canonical-abbreviation judge drops the section, so its own repair can never run
proposals.defect: The judge constructs Failure("COMPOSING", ...) without the `section` field that Failure's own docstring (registry.py:200-211) calls the field that routes it. COMPOSING maps to S6, which repair/targeted.py:192-200 treats as repairable only when some failure names an LLM-owned section; with section_id None it rewrites the stage to None and records 'no failing check names an LLM-owned section'. The check is structurally unrepairable - a permanent unrepairable finding blocking a candidate, which loop-prompt.md section 6 rule 5 prohibits.
proposals.section_is_knowable: _section_texts() - already called four times in the same function ten lines above - places the offending word in additional_examples, an LLM-owned section.
proposals.control: BC-08 in the same run, same repairer, same candidate, repaired on attempt 1 because its judge did set section.
proposals.alternative_rejected: Widening _LOWER_WORD's lookbehind to (?<![-.\w]) so a hyphenated slug never fires: suppresses the symptom, leaves the routing hole for every other abbreviation, and would silently admit a README that spells an identifier as prose.
proposals.not_asked_for: No weakening of BC-07. The content defect underneath - an identifier written as bare prose rather than a code span - is real and the check is right to refuse it.
proposals.reversal: If BC-07's structure failures are deliberately unroutable, the abbreviation sub-check is in the wrong check and should move to an S6-judged check instead.

proposals.title: seed_call_store cannot seed a batched job, so no multi-batch repository can ever prove its no-op
proposals.defect: seed_call_store seeds a job only when its sealed calls.jsonl holds exactly one successful attempt (`if len(attempts) != 1 ... continue`). _SEEDABLE_JOBS maps source_reconciliation to dispositions.json, but S4 is batched by design: reconciliation_batches() splits the inherited units, one call per batch, and merge_dispositions() merges them into the single artifact. N batches produce N successful attempts as the normal shape. The docstring's stated reason - a repair round re-asking the same job, where only the last attempt is genuine - is sound for a re-ask and false for a batch, and the rule cannot tell them apart.
proposals.measured_consequence: Cells' sealed ledger holds source_reconciliation: 2 successful attempts, so S4 was not seeded; the rerun made a live call, a non-deterministic model returned different dispositions, that changed the planning packet so even the seeded presentation_planning key missed, and the divergence carried through to REJECT_PRESENTATION.
proposals.scope: Any repository whose reconciliation needs more than one batch. Measured this run: PDF 3 batches, Page 3, Cells 2. Only a single-batch repository can seed S4 today.
proposals.alternative_rejected: Seeding from the last successful attempt: restores the exact lie the docstring guards against for genuine re-asks, and is still wrong for batches, where no single attempt's output equals the merged artifact. The honest fix keys each batch's own logical_call_id to that batch's own output, which means the bundle must carry per-batch reconciliation outputs - a bundle-format change, and the primary's to design.
proposals.reversal: If S4 is not meant to be seedable, remove it from _SEEDABLE_JOBS and restate loop-prompt section 3's 'byte-identical with zero provider calls' to the number of batch calls a no-op legitimately costs - explicitly, rather than by silent failure.
proposals.a_second_distinct_mechanism: 40f2e9d's portfolio-wide proposal reports that no candidate sealed since 352fd35 can pass a no-op proof because run_job re-judges a stored S4 reply against the decoder's enum while normalize writes IDs the packet never showed. That is NOT E5: E5 is about a batched S4 never being seeded so a live call is made; lane B's is about a stored reply being re-judged and refused. They compound - a single-batch job that cleared E5 would still meet lane B's. Lane E does not claim lane B's mechanism and has not measured it; the two entries should be read together.

proposals.title: The S4 fact_ids fix was not applied to its four sibling sites at S5, and that is Page for Python's live blocker
proposals.defect: 352fd35 fixed reconciliation_schema's fact_ids by pinning it to an enum of the packet's own IDs. The identical field name, in the identical role, at the sibling S5 site, was not fixed - at four places: core_capabilities.items.fact_ids, api_hubs.items.fact_ids, material_limitations.items.fact_ids and deviations.items.fact_ids are each a bare {type: array, items: {type: string}}, and planning_schema() rewrites none of them. Inside one object, planning_schema() does replace api_hubs.items.symbol_fact_id with an enum and leaves its immediate sibling fact_ids accepting any string.
proposals.finding: rejected twice at S5 on 'unknown fact ID public_symbol:aspose.page.xps.renderer', found at exactly api_hubs[2].fact_ids[5] in calls/910e76cb940e.rejected-2.json. The same invention the G3 second pass recorded for this repository as public_symbol:aspose.page.common.
proposals.consequence_for_the_lane_file: Page's recorded class did not survive item 40 - it moved from S4 to S5. It was never an S4-only class but a fact_ids-shaped hole at both stages. The lane file's expectation that 'item 40 other half (symbol_kinds bounding) cites it by name' is not sufficient: symbol_fact_id bounding is already in place and is not what failed.
proposals.fix_has_a_working_model: citable_fact_ids() already computes the exact citable set from bounded_records(), and planning_schema() already uses bounded_records() for its other enums under Taskcard H's cap.
proposals.size_objection_answered: Three live measurements this run: 689/34,409 (PDF), 360/17,119 (Page), 252/12,590 (Cells) across 8 S4 calls, every one HTTP 200 on attempt 1. Taskcard H's confirmed 400 was at ~24,830 symbols with no bounded_records cap at all.
proposals.alternative_rejected: Leaving the four fields free and relying on binding_errors plus a prompt sentence. That is what is in place now and what the G3 second pass already tried to fix by prompt wording; it costs two full S5 calls and a dead run per repository. Section 27.5 D1's point is that the schema should make the mistake unrepresentable.
proposals.reversal: If a bounded enum at these four sites trips a 400 on a larger-surface repository, the answer is Taskcard H's - tighten bounded_records' cap for this packet - never a return to a free string array.

proposals.title: The seal sorts facts by ID, the renderer does not sort at all, so a sealed README can be unrenderable from its own sealed facts
proposals.defect: FactsDocument.to_json writes `sorted(self.facts, key=lambda f: f.id)`, while the renderer emits dependency bullets with `lines.extend(f"- `{fact.value}`" for fact in required)` and no sort. The live pipeline renders from the in-memory document in EXTRACTION order; the replay renders from facts.json in ID order. Wherever the two disagree for any two facts in one rendered list, the sealed bytes cannot be reproduced from the sealed facts - by construction, on the first try.
proposals.severity: Outranks E5: E5 costs the no-op proof, E7 costs the commit. This is why the run lands no candidate.
proposals.scope: Data-dependent - eight bundles pass this test and the ninth does not. It bites when a manifest declares dependencies in non-alphabetical order, and the dependency bullets are only the list this run happened to hit; the same asymmetry applies to every unsorted lines.extend(... for fact in ...) in the renderer.
proposals.alternative_rejected: Sorting the dependency bullets in the renderer: fixes this one list, leaves the general asymmetry, and silently changes the presentation order of every existing candidate - a manifest's own declaration order is arguably the better reading order. The narrower fix is to make the seal preserve the order the render consumed.
proposals.reversal: If test_sealed_bytes is too strict - a sealed bundle need only be semantically, not byte-, reproducible - then the check is what changes. It should not be left as is: today it silently converts an accepted candidate into an unlandable one.
proposals.independent_corroboration: 40f2e9d (lane B, G4-W13-RERUN2, landed the same day) hit the identical class from the other side: test_sealed_bytes caught declared_dependencies sorted by the manifest spelling while fact IDs are slugged, so the sealed README listed Python3 before googletest and a re-render listed them the other way. Same test, same section, same two-line transposition, same manifest-order-versus-ID-order cause.
proposals.precedent_for_the_fix: Lane B fixed it in its OWN C++ plugin, with a mutation test, because it owned the producer. Lane E cannot do the same: the Python extractor is shared and mature, so this stays a proposal. The owner has a measured choice the two lanes now frame together - fix each producer one ecosystem at a time as 40f2e9d did, or make the two shared sites (core/facts.py:136 and renderer.py:263) agree once so no future plugin can reintroduce it. Lane E has no standing to pick and records the evidence for both.
